question: The All India Chess Federation (AICF) launched which scheme to support young chess players from U-7 to U-19 age groups in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Top National Players Stipend Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **All India Chess Federation (AICF)** introduced the **Top National Players Stipend Scheme** in early **2025** as a landmark initiative to provide financial stability to budding chess prodigies across **India**.
 
• This scheme is specifically designed to support young players in age groups ranging from **Under-7 (U-7)** to **Under-19 (U-19)**, covering both **Open** and **Girls** categories.
 
• Under this initiative, the **top 12 players** from each national age-group championship are eligible to receive a monthly stipend, creating a pool of approximately **156 beneficiaries** annually.
 
• The financial aid is intended to cover essential expenses such as **professional coaching**, **travel for international tournaments**, and **entry fees**, helping players focus on their growth without economic pressure.
 
• The implementation of this scheme in **2025** aligns with the **AICF's** broader vision to maintain India's dominance in world chess following the country's historic **Double Gold** win at the **45th Chess Olympiad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **All India Chess Federation (AICF):**
 
 
• Established in **1951**, the **AICF** is the central administrative body for chess in **India** and is headquartered in **New Delhi**.
 
• It is affiliated with **FIDE** (International Chess Federation) and has been instrumental in producing over **80 Grandmasters** as of **2024-2025**.
 
• The current leadership, including President **Nitin Narang** and Secretary **Dev A. Patel**, has focused on grassroots development and administrative transparency.
 
 
 
• **Chess Development in India:**
 
 
• India has emerged as a global superpower in chess, boasting world-class talents like **D Gukesh**, **Arjun Erigaisi**, and **R Praggnanandhaa**.
 
• The **Top National Players Stipend Scheme** is part of a larger **₹65 crore** budget allocated for the **2024-2025** cycle to revamp the chess ecosystem.
 
• Other recent initiatives include the **National Chess Academy** and the introduction of **Chess in Schools** programs to popularize the game at the primary level.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Stipend Schemes:**
 
 
• By providing a **stipend**, the federation aims to prevent "talent drain," where high-potential players quit the sport due to the high costs associated with **Grandmaster**-level training.
 
• This structured support system acts as a **scholarship**, rewarding consistency in **National Championships** and encouraging competitive participation at the state and district levels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Top National Players Stipend Scheme** is a merit-based system where performance in the **National Age Group Championships** serves as the sole criteria for selection.
 
• The stipend amounts are tiered, ensuring that those ranked higher (e.g., **Rank 1 to 3**) receive a more significant portion of the **financial aid** compared to those in the lower bracket of the top 12.
 
• This initiative marks the first time in **Indian Chess** history that such a large number of junior players are being brought under a direct **monthly payroll** by the national federation.
 
• The scheme also complements the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**' efforts under the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**, which primarily focuses on senior elite athletes.
